name: Tilaknagar Industries Ltd
title: Tilaknagar Industries Ltd-$ - 507205 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Volumes up 135% in Q4 on Imperial Blue acquisition, but growth is acquisition-driven; ex-IB Q4 volume flat and utilisation/capacity signals are thin, with FY27 guidance of HSD-LDD volume growth and 16-18% EBITDA margin over 24-36 months.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 148% YoY to INR 949 crore and EBITDA margin was 16.3%, with Imperial Blue consolidated; FY27 guided to 16-18% combined EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes rose 135% YoY to over 8 million cases, of which Imperial Blue (IB) contributed 4.6 million cases, while ex-IB volumes were roughly flat as Andhra Pradesh base effects reversed. Reported net revenue was INR 949 crore (INR 941 crore subsidy-adjusted) and EBITDA was INR 155 crore at a 16.3% margin, or INR 146 crore and 15.5% subsidy-adjusted. Management changed presentation so trade discounts and schemes are netted from gross revenue, which lowers reported revenue and gross margin but lifts EBITDA and PAT margins without changing absolute figures. FY27 guidance covers high-single to low-double digit volume growth and a 16-18% combined EBITDA margin over 24-36 months.

financial_highlights.change: +5.4% vs INR 1,116 in Q4 FY25; ex-IB NSR +2.6%
Mainly TSMA fees and labour code impact

segments.name: Imperial Blue (IB)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume of 4.6 million cases; ex-Maharashtra growth about 9% YoY. H2 is about 52% of IB volumes. Management does not disclose brand-wise NSR; IB NSR is said to be about INR 20-30 above combined NSR under the new presentation.

segments.name: Ex-IB base business (TI)
segments.commentary: Ex-IB volumes were flat in Q4 against a high Andhra Pradesh base from the route-to-market change in Oct/Nov 2024; secondary sales grew about 5%. FY26 ex-IB volume was 13.6 million cases, up 14%.

segments.name: Mansion House brandy
segments.commentary: Crossed 10 million cases in FY26 and is India's largest P&A brandy. TI holds close to 40% P&A IMFL share in Southern India in Q4 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth of high-single digit to low-double digit for the combined business, then double-digit volume growth over the next couple of years; double-digit volume CAGR over 3 years.
Combined EBITDA margin of 16-18% over the next 24-36 months, with 15.5% FY26 as the base; the lower end implies about 50 bps improvement.
Net debt to EBITDA below 1.0x by FY29; net debt of about INR 1,700 crore by March 2027.
Capex about INR 25 crore each in FY27 and FY28, maintenance only.
TSMA fees to decline quarter on quarter, with a full-year FY27 impact of INR 55-60 crore; all TSMA states to transition by March 2027.
Working capital cycle of 53-55 days of gross revenue on an ongoing basis.
Combined-business margin benefit of 60-100 bps from the India-UK FTA scotch duty cut, mostly on IB; Telangana price increase is possible but timing is unknown.
Q1 FY27 margins expected to see some short-term pressure from input cost inflation.
capex_capacity: Prag (Andhra Pradesh) bottling capacity raised from 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases per annum after government approval; investment about INR 59 crore, fully spent; bottling savings of about INR 10 crore per year expected.
Nigeria subsidiary investment of up to INR 30 crore; existing business about 2.5 lakh cases.
Shrirampur ENA distillery was under qualification issues; recommissioning investment is under consideration with no timing set.
Capex of about INR 25 crore a year in FY27-FY28, maintenance only.
demand_pricing: Karnataka excise policy cut consumer prices of Imperial Blue and Mansion House by about INR 20 per 180 ml nip; previous Karnataka cut (INR 257 to INR 235 per nip) drove growth there above high teens.
Telangana dues stable in days since January; management is working with the government to reduce outstanding days.
Brandy P&A (prestige and above) expected to grow at a similar clip to TI's overall growth; northern brandy launch planned in FY27.
Selling expenses under the new presentation are about 6-6.5% of grossed-up revenue, per management.
Amara Vodka (SSL portfolio) expected to gain traction from the usership arrangement.

Q4 FY26 NSR up 5.4% to INR 1,177 per case; a Karan Kamdar estimate of IB at about INR 2,400 crore annualised revenue was described as directionally right with the NSR adjusted for the accounting change.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ex-IB volume flat in Q4, and what is IB seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY25 Andhra Pradesh sales were inflated by the route-to-market change; secondary ex-IB growth was about 5%. IB is fairly evenly spread across quarters, with H2 about 52% of volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 250-400 bps margin expansion comes from the India-UK FTA duty cut versus operational initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: The duty cut is worth 60-100 bps on the combined business, mostly on IB. The rest comes from cost optimisation and possible price increases, including Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IB run rate and the growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: IB growth should be similar to or slightly above the combined business because of its lower FY26 base; Maharashtra impact is largely in the FY26 base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 IB NSR?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand-wise NSR is not disclosed. Under the new net-of-selling-expense presentation, IB NSR is about INR 20-30 above the combined NSR.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no gross debt guidance, and what is net debt at March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is less relevant because of a 2-year moratorium; net debt is expected at about INR 1,700 crore by March 2027, with upside bias.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin path and the Q1 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management uses 15.5% as the base. The full year should hold the guided range, but Q1 FY27 faces input cost inflation, so no Q1 expansion is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Will TSMA costs keep hitting operating expenses after transition?
qa_highlights.answer: No. TSMA is treated as an exceptional item, and only about 5% of the cost is expected to recur in operating expenses.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation tied to the geopolitical situation, with Q1 FY27 margin pressure acknowledged.
TSMA transition: 3 states remain, with one likely to continue into H2 FY27; outer date March 2027. April 2026 saw small disruptions after exits.
Telangana receivable days and possible price increase timing unclear.
Accounting change lowers reported revenue; FY27 revenue of more than INR 5,000 crore including brandy is now said to be below that level.
Deferred consideration of EUR 28 million payable to Pernod Ricard after 4 years.
Shrirampur ENA distillery qualification issue unresolved, with no investment timeline.
Karnataka and Maharashtra policy effects on volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and margin targets and on integration progress, but cautious on Q1 FY27 margins because of input cost inflation. Management was evasive on brand-level NSR, TSMA state names and new launches, and on the Pernod-related revenue baseline.
key_quotes: To be very frank, we are not giving an NSR segregation on a brand-wise basis.
So any kind of inflationary impact is going to be taken care of at the lower range of our guidance.
So these are all significantly, what do you say, extraordinary items itself.
We would be transitioned by end of FY27 itself. I do not see any reason for any kind of delays on that front.

growth.why: FY27 guided to high-single to low-double digit combined volume growth and 16-18% EBITDA margin over 24-36 months; backing is partial, with Prag bottling capacity raised to 36 lakh cases (INR 59 crore, fully spent) and IB volumes contributing, but no contracted or quantified order book, and ex-IB volumes were flat in Q4 against a high base.
